Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:11:1.hebrew: משום דלא קתני כמה שהזיק - הא לאו תיובתא היא, דלא פסיקא ליה למיתני כמה שהזיק דליהוי משמע דפחות אינו משלם ע"פ עצמו, כיון דאיכא חצי נזק צרורות דאינו משלם כמה שהזיק, ואפילו הכי משלם ע"פ עצמו, דהלכתא גמירי לה דממונא הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:11:1.english: Because it does not teach "as much as he damaged" - This is not a refutation, for it was not categorical for [the Tanna] to teach "as much as he damaged" such that it would imply that [where one pays] less, he does not pay by his own admission, since there is [the case of] half-damage [caused by] pebbles, where he does not pay as much as he damaged, and even so he pays by his own admission, because it is a traditional law that it is monetary [restitution].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:13:2.hebrew: משונה הוא - דאין דרכן בכך, והוי תולדה דקרן לשלם חצי נזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:13:2.english: It is atypical - For it is not their way [to do] so, and it is a derivative of Goring, [requiring the owner] to pay half-damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:13:3.hebrew: ולא מגבינן לה בבבל - דאין דנין דיני קנסות אלא בסמוכין, ובבבל אין סמיכה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:13:3.english: And we do not collect it in Babylonia - For cases of fines are adjudicated only by ordained [judges], and in Babylonia there is no ordination.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:14:1.hebrew: ברברבי - תרנגולים וכבשים גדולים, דאין דרך כלב וחתול להורגן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:14:1.english: Large [animals] - Large chickens and sheep, for it is not the way of a dog or a cat to kill them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:15:1.hebrew: ואי תפיס - ניזק בבבל, לא מפקינן מיניה: ואי לא תפיס ניזק, ואמר: "קבעו לי זמן דליתי בהדי לארעא דישראל", קבעינן ליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:15:1.english: And if he seized - [If] the injured party [seized property] in Babylonia, we do not reclaim [it] from him. And if the injured party did not seize [property], and he said, "Set a time for me that he should come with me to the Land of Israel," we set [a time] for him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:17:1.english: And either way, we excommunicate him - to kill the dog and the cat.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:17:2.english: Until he removes the danger - That he kills them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:1:1.hebrew: המית שורי כו' מאי לאו בתם - וה"ק: המית שורי את פלוני, משלם חצי כופר ע"פ עצמו, ורבי יוסי הגלילי היא; או שורו של פלוני המית, משלם ע"פ עצמו חצי נזק. אלמא ממונא הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:1:1.english: My ox killed, etc.; is it not [referring] to a tam [ox] - And this is what [the Mishnah] is saying: [If one says,] "My ox killed so-and-so," he pays half-ransom based on his own [admission] — and this is [the view of] Rabbi Yosei HaGelili — or [if he says,] "[My ox] killed so-and-so's ox," he pays half-damages based on his own [admission]. Apparently, [half-damages] is monetary [compensation].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:20:1.english: Not to gore - with the horn.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:20:2.hebrew: ולא ליגוף - דחיפת גוף. וכולהו הוי תולדה דקרן ומשלמין חצי נזק, הרי חמשה תמין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:20:2.english: Nor for pushing - Pushing with [its] body. And all of them are a subcategory of Horn and pay half-damages; behold, [there are] five innocuous [cases].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:21:1.hebrew: ושור המועד - ג' פעמים ליגח, או לגוף, או לרבוץ, או לבעוט, או לשוך — הרי הן חמשה מועדין לשלם נזק שלם; ולגבי מועד חשיב להו חד, דע"י העדאה דעדים אתי בהו חיוב נ"ש, הלכך חדא מילתא הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:21:1.english: And the forewarned ox - [That acted] three times to gore, or to push, or to crouch, or to kick, or to bite — behold, these are five forewarned [categories] to pay full damages. And with respect to [counting] "forewarned," [the Mishnah] considers them one, because the obligation of full damages comes to them through forewarning by witnesses; therefore, it is one matter.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:21:2.hebrew: ושור המזיק ברשות הניזק - ואפי' קרן תמה הוי כמועד לשלם נזק שלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:21:2.english: And an ox that causes damage on the property of the injured [party] - And even an innocuous horn [is considered] like a forewarned [ox] to pay full damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:21:3.hebrew: והאדם - הרי חמשה. ובבעלי חיים קמיירי, להכי לא חשיב בור ואש; ולקמן פריך: אמאי לא חשיב הארי והדוב כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:21:3.english: And the person - Behold, [these are] five. And [the Mishnah] is speaking of living creatures; therefore it does not count a pit or fire. And later [the Gemara] asks: Why does it not count the lion and the bear, etc.?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:22:1.hebrew: הרי אלו מועדים - אפילו בנשיכה ובכל נזקין, ומשלמין בעלים שלהן נזק שלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:22:1.english: These are forewarned - Even for biting and for all damages, and their owners pay full damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:22:2.english: That they are domesticated - [Meaning] that a person raised them in his home.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:23:1.hebrew: וקתני הבהמה אינה מועדת - לא ליגח ולא לגוף, אלמא קרן בחצר הניזק חצי נזק הוא דמשלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:23:1.english: And it teaches: The animal is not forewarned - Neither to gore nor to push; thus, [for] Horn in the courtyard of the injured party, it is half-damages that [the owner] pays.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:3:1.hebrew: עבדו של פלוני - הא קנסא הוא, דמשלם ל' סלעים, ואפילו אינו שוה אלא דינר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:3:1.english: So-and-so’s slave - This is a fine, for he pays thirty selaim, even if [the slave] is worth only a dinar.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:3:2.english: Let [the mishna] differentiate and teach [the distinction] with regard to [that case] itself - In the first [clause] itself, of "My ox killed so-and-so's ox," it could have differentiated.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:5:1.english: The entire [mishna] speaks of a forewarned [ox] - And [it] wishes to teach us the distinctions of a forewarned [ox].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:6:1.hebrew: יותר על מה שהזיק - כגון ל' של עבד:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:6:1.english: More than that which he damaged - For example, the thirty [shekels] of a slave:

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:6:2.hebrew: הא פחות - כגון חצי נזק דתם, משלם ע"פ עצמו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:6:2.english: But less - such as half-damage of an innocuous [ox], he pays based on his own [admission].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 15b:7:1.english: As much as that which he damaged - Full damages of a forewarned [damager].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 15b:13:1.hebrew: והשתא דאמרת פלגא נזקא קנסא - נראה דדוקא למ"ד פלגא דנזקא קנסא, אבל למ"ד פלגא דנזקא ממונא לא מיחייב כלל, דמהי תיתי? דמקרן לא אתיא, דקרן אורחיה הוא — דסתם שוורים לאו בחזקת שימור קיימי; והאי משונה הוא, דלאו אורחיה דכלבא למיכל אימרי רברבי. אבל למ"ד פלגא נזקא קנסא, הוי תולדה דקרן, דתרוייהו משונים הם, אע"ג דקרן כוונתו להזיק:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 15b:13:1.english: "And now that you have said that half-damage is a fine" - It seems that [this applies] specifically according to the one who says half-damage is a fine, but according to the one who says half-damage is monetary [compensation], he is not liable at all, for from where would [liability] come? For it cannot be derived from Keren [Goring], since Keren is [considered] its normal way — as ordinary oxen are not presumed to be guarded; whereas this is unusual, since it is not the normal way of a dog to eat large lambs. But according to the one who says half-damage is a fine, it is a derivative of Keren, since both of them are unusual, even though [in] Keren its intent is to damage.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 15b:15:1.hebrew: ואי תפס לא מפקינן מיניה - אור"ת, דוקא אי תפס [המזיק עצמו כגון] כלב או השונרא קאמר דלא מפקינן, דבמזיק הקילו חכמים שיוכל להחזיק בו אם לקחו בשעת ההיזק; אבל מידי אחרינא לא, דאי בכל דבר שיתפוס לא מפקינן — יבא לידי תקלה, דהיום או למחר יגזול כל אשר לו ולא נוציא ממנו, דאין אנו דנין דיני קנסות, וזה יפסיד יותר ממה שהזיק. והא דאמר בכיצד הרגל (לקמן בבא קמא דף יט:): "ההוא חמרא דאכל נהמא ופלסיה לסלא, וחייביה רב יהודה אנהמא נזק שלם ואסלא חצי נזק" — מיירי בתפס, או היה דוחקו ע"י שמתא דקבעיה זימנא לא"י:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 15b:15:1.english: And if he seized [it], we do not reclaim [it] from him - Rabbeinu Tam says: [The Gemara] specifically means that if he seized [the damager itself, such as] a dog or the cat, we do not reclaim [it], for regarding the damager [itself] the Sages were lenient, [allowing] that he may keep it if he took it at the time of the damage; but regarding anything else, [we do] not [allow him to keep it], for if regarding anything he might seize we would not reclaim [it] — it would lead to a mishap, for today or tomorrow he will rob everything that belongs to him and we will not exact [it] from him, since we do not adjudicate cases of fines, and this [person] will lose more than what [his animal] damaged. And that which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Keitzad HaRegel (below, Bava Kamma 19b): "A certain donkey ate bread and broke the basket, and Rav Yehudah obligated [its owner] for the bread [to pay] full damages, and for the basket half damages" — [that] refers to a case where [the injured party] seized [payment], or [where Rav Yehudah] pressured him by means of a ban of excommunication, [in] that he set a time for him [to appear] in the Land of Israel.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 15b:22:1.hebrew: והנחש הרי אלו מועדים - לאו בכל עניני היזק חשיבי מועדים, אלא כל אחד במידי דאורחיה: כגון שבא זאב וטרף, ארי ודרס או טרף להניח. אבל במידי דלאו אורחיה, כגון ארי שטרף ואכל, וכן שאר הזיקות דלאו אורחייהו — לא הוו מועדים, אלא משלמי' ח"נ. ובמידי דאורחייהו, דמשלם נ"ש, היינו דוקא בחצר הניזק, אבל ברה"ר פטור, דהוי שן ברה"ר, כדאמר שמואל בגמ': "ארי ברה"ר דרס ואכל — פטור". ואפי' נחש, שאין נהנה מנשיכתו — כדאמרינן בפ"ק דתענית (דף ח.) שנתקבצו כל החיות אצל הנחש ואומרות לו: "מה הנאה יש לך?" — מ"מ, כיון דאורחיה בהכי, הוי כמו רגל ופטור ברה"ר, ולא הוי כמו קרן בתר דאייעד, אע"פ דמתכוין להזיק, מדחשיב ליה גבי אחריני:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 15b:22:1.english: And the snake — these are forewarned - They are not considered forewarned with respect to all types of damage, but rather each one [is forewarned] for what is its normal way [of causing damage]: for example, where a wolf came and tore [prey], [or] a lion trampled or tore [prey] to leave [it for later]. However, for something that is not its normal way, such as a lion that tore and ate [prey], and similarly the other [types of] damages that are not their normal way — they are not [considered] forewarned, but rather pay half-damages. And for something that is their normal way, where [the owner] pays full damages, that is specifically in the injured party's courtyard, whereas in the public domain he is exempt, for it is [categorized as] Tooth in the public domain, as Shmuel says in the Gemara: "A lion in the public domain that trampled and ate — he is exempt." And even a snake, which derives no benefit from its bite — as we say in the first chapter of Taanit (8a) that all the beasts gathered around the snake and said to it, "What benefit do you have?" — nevertheless, since its normal way is [to act] like this, it is like Foot and is exempt in the public domain, and it is not like Horn after it has been attested [as forewarned], even though it intends to cause damage, since [the Mishnah] lists it together with the others.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 15b:22:2.hebrew: רבי אלעזר אומר בזמן שהן בני תרבות אינן מועדים - תימה, דבריש פ"ק דסנהדרין (דף ב. ושם) תנן: "הארי והזאב והדוב כו', ר"א אומר: כל הקודם להורגו זכה", ומפרש ר' יוחנן בגמ' (שם טו:): אע"פ שלא המיתו, דאין להם תרבות ואין להם בעלים. ואור"י, דהכא גרסינן ר' אלעזר, שהוא אחר ר' מאיר, והתם גרסינן ר' אליעזר, שהוא קודם ר' עקיבא, דקתני בתריה "ר' עקיבא אומר". מיהו אכתי קשה: דהתנן "והנחש מועד לעולם" — אליבא דכ"ע, והתם מפרש ריש לקיש: והוא שהמיתו, אבל לא המיתו — לא; קסבר יש להם תרבות ויש להם בעלים אפי' אנחש. ואומר ר"ת, דהתם — בקשורים בשלשלאות, כגון ארי בגוהרקי שלו, דבענין זה יש להם תרבות [ואין להם להרגם אא"כ המיתו, ותרבות דהכא היינו שגידלם בביתו]. ועוד יש לחלק: דוקא לענין זה יש להם תרבות, שאין להם להרגם כל הקודם אא"כ המיתו; אבל לענין אם הזיקו, לשלם נזק שלם או לא — בהא לא איירי מידי אם חשיב תרבות שלהם תרבות:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 15b:22:2.english: Rabbi Elazar says: When they are domesticated they are not forewarned - This is astonishing, for at the beginning of the first chapter of Sanhedrin (2a and there [in the chapter]) we learned [in a Mishnah]: "The lion, the wolf, the bear, etc. Rabbi Eliezer says: Whoever is first to kill them acquires [merit]." And Rabbi Yochanan explains in the Gemara (ibid., 15b): [This applies] even if they have not killed [anyone], because they cannot be domesticated and they have no owners. And Rabbi Yitzchak says that here [in our Mishnah] we read "Rabbi Elazar," who came after Rabbi Meir, whereas there [in Sanhedrin] we read "Rabbi Eliezer," who preceded Rabbi Akiva, for it teaches after him: "Rabbi Akiva says." However, it is still difficult, for our Mishnah teaches "And the snake is always forewarned" — according to all [opinions]; yet there [in Sanhedrin] Reish Lakish explains: [They may be killed] provided that they have killed, but if they have not killed, [they may] not [be killed] — [meaning] he holds they can be domesticated and they have owners, even [with respect to] a snake. And Rabbeinu Tam says that there [in Sanhedrin, it is speaking] of [animals] tied with chains, such as a lion in its cage, for in this manner they can be domesticated (and one may not kill them unless they have killed, whereas the domestication [here] means that he raised them in his house). And one can also distinguish [between the two]: Specifically with regard to this matter — that whoever is first may not kill them unless they have killed — they are considered domesticated; but with regard to [the case where] they caused damage, whether to pay full damages or not — regarding this, [the Gemara in Sanhedrin] does not discuss at all whether their domestication is considered domestication.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 15b:3:1.hebrew: לפלוג וליתני בדידיה בד"א במועד אבל בתם כו' - תימה: היכי הוה מצי למימר הכי — "אבל בתם אין משלם ע"פ עצמו", דמשמע דע"פ עדים משלם כשהמית שורו את פלוני? דלמא לא סבר כרבי יוסי הגלילי, דאמר: תם משלם חצי כופר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 15b:3:1.english: "Let [the Mishnah] differentiate and teach [the distinction] with regard to [the first case] itself: In what case are these words said? With a forewarned [ox], but with an innocuous [ox], etc." - This is astonishing: how could [the Gemara] have said this — "but with an innocuous [ox] he does not pay based on his own [admission]," which implies that based on [the testimony of] witnesses he does pay when his ox killed so-and-so? Perhaps [the Tanna] does not hold like Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who says that an innocuous [ox] pays half-ransom [kofer].
